Overall, ITME enhances conventional CPU-offloading by providing additional remote memory expansion to accommodate large KV cache footprints beyond host memory limits, achieving up to a 35.7% throughput improvement. [...] ITME implements differentiated fallback policies for cache misses. While a model weight miss inevitably triggers a pipeline stall, a KV cache miss is resolved through dynamic recomputation on the GPU. This design choice avoids the inefficiency of retrieving isolated missing blocks from the remote tier, which would necessitate either suboptimal chunk-sized transfers or complex retrieval logic. Consequently, recomputing the missing KV segments directly on the GPU is more performance-efficient [...] mitigates memory capacity and I/O bottlenecks through software prefetching and read-priority scheduling. Overall, ITME enhances conventional CPU-offloading by providing the necessary memory expansion to accommodate large KV cache footprints beyond host memory limits, achieving up to a 35.7% throughput improvement.

Investor Outlook:  
The Korean rally highlights both opportunity and risk. On the bullish side, SK Hynix and Samsung are uniquely positioned to capture the next leg of AI investment, supported by structural supply advantages and political leverage as essential partners to U.S. tech firms. Longer-term, sustained demand for HBM chips could transform the cyclical memory business into a more stable growth engine. [...] patterns of memory markets, potentially smoothing revenue streams that have long been hostage to consumer electronics cycles. [...] The latest surge in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix underscores how quickly the race for artificial intelligence hardware is reshaping the semiconductor sector. After OpenAI’s Sam Altman signed preliminary agreements with the two Korean heavyweights, shares of SK Hynix climbed more than 12% to multiyear highs while Samsung gained around 5%, adding over $30 billion in combined market capitalization and pulling the Kospi index to a record.

results.title: Why Micron and SK Hynix Could Quietly Become the Real AI Winners
results.content:
With a favorable demand environment for their offerings and strong technological advantages, both Micron and SK Hynix are well positioned to keep capturing a significant share of this growing and profitable market.

## Should you buy stock in Micron Technology right now?

Before you buy stock in Micron Technology, consider this: [...] Within that dynamic, leading memory players such as Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) and SK Hynix (OTC: HXSCL) -- already crucial players in the global buildout of AI infrastructure -- are well-positioned to prosper.

## Favorable memory market trends [...] So naturally, data center companies are increasing their spending on memory as part of their ongoing AI infrastructure buildouts. The global HBM market is forecast to grow from $17 billion in 2024 to $98 billion in 2030, while HBM's revenue share in the DRAM market is estimated to grow from 18% to 50% in that same time frame. This trend favors Micron and SK Hynix, which stand to benefit from the higher memory content of systems designed to handle large, scalable AI workloads.
